project_title: Network-Assisted Detection and Reconstruction of Cyber Incidents under Anti-Forensic Conditions

research_scope.objective: Evaluate whether independent network evidence improves cyber-incident reconstruction when host evidence is degraded by anti-forensic activity.
research_scope.research_question: To what extent does network evidence improve incident reconstruction completeness and accuracy as host evidence undergoes increasing levels of anti-forensic degradation?
research_scope.scope: One controlled file-access and simulated-exfiltration scenario.

scenarios.name: Unauthorized File Access and Simulated Exfiltration
scenarios.description: Controlled creation, access, reading, local staging, and network transfer of a synthetic test file to a designated laboratory receiver.

degradation_levels.name: Low
degradation_levels.description: Low-level degradation of selected non-critical host evidence.

degradation_levels.name: Moderate
degradation_levels.description: Removal of selected non-critical evidence and controlled host timestamp modification.

degradation_levels.name: High
degradation_levels.description: Additional host log-record removal alongside L2 operations.

degradation_levels.name: Severe
degradation_levels.description: Additional alteration of selected host log timestamps alongside L3 operations.

evidence_policy.host_evidence: Collected from the Windows incident execution system.

v2.0_reserved.description: Expanded scenarios, automated evidence pipelines, larger experimental dataset, and additional validation.
